subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
passage: It was nearly midnight in the student residence in Melbourne when Gabriel banged on the door. "Your music! Every single night! Are you deaf?" He stood in the doorway, face red, voice bouncing down the corridor. Tuan's stomach dropped. For a second he felt pinned, then a hot urge rose in his arms to shove Gabriel back out. Instead he stepped back into the room, putting the desk between them, and switched off the speaker. "Okay. It's off," he said, keeping his voice low and level. "I'm not going to shout." Gabriel kept going for a bit: exams, no sleep, this whole floor. Tuan didn't answer back. Gradually Gabriel's voice dropped. He rubbed his eyes. "I've got a test at eight," he muttered. "Sorry for yelling." "Let's talk tomorrow about quiet hours," Tuan said.

qa.q: What did Tuan put between himself and Gabriel?
qa.a: Tuan put the desk between them.

qa.q: What did Tuan feel when Gabriel banged on the door?
qa.a: Tuan felt shock and fear, then a hot urge to shove Gabriel back out; his stomach dropped.

qa.q: Why did keeping distance and a low voice work?
qa.a: It kept things safe and gave Gabriel nothing to push against, so his anger ran out and he apologised.

qa.q: What was going on for Gabriel that night?
qa.a: Gabriel was exhausted and stressed, with a test at eight and no sleep, which fed his shouting.

grounding: A young adult shouted at in a residence feels shock and an urge to hit back, but keeps distance and a low voice until the other person deflates.

subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
passage: In the hostel common room, Pradeep yanked open the fridge and turned on Parveen. "You ate my dabba again! Admit it!" He took two steps toward her, his voice cracking loud. Parveen's heart jumped into her throat. She had not touched his food, and part of her wanted to scream right back in his face. Instead she moved toward the open doorway, keeping the long table between them. "I didn't take it," she said evenly. "I'm not going to shout. I'll talk when you're calmer." Two juniors by the TV had gone silent. Pradeep yelled another sentence, then another, but with no one shouting back, the words ran out. He stood there breathing hard. The next morning a note on the fridge read: "Found my dabba in Room 12. Sorry, Parveen. P."

qa.q: Where did Pradeep find his dabba?
qa.a: Pradeep found his dabba in Room 12.

qa.q: What did Parveen feel when Pradeep stepped toward her?
qa.a: Parveen felt fear, with her heart jumping into her throat, and also a strong wish to scream back.

qa.q: Which choices kept Parveen safe?
qa.a: Moving toward the open doorway, keeping the table between them and refusing to match his volume.

qa.q: How might the two juniors by the TV have felt?
qa.a: They were likely tense and uneasy, going silent as the shouting grew.

grounding: A young adult on the receiving end of shouting keeps her distance and refuses to match the volume, and the other person runs out of steam.

subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
passage:
Hostel warden's note, girls' block, Sunday night
At 11 pm I heard shouting from room 214. Kavitha was yelling at her roommate Nikita about a missing charger, loud enough for the whole corridor. I went up. Nikita was standing near the open door, well back from Kavitha, arms at her sides. She looked shaken, but her voice stayed quiet. 'I didn't take it. I'll talk when you're not shouting.' Kavitha shouted again. Nikita didn't raise her voice. She just said, 'I'm going to wait in the corridor.' Within a couple of minutes Kavitha sat down on her bed and started crying about her exam tomorrow. I sat with them both. The charger was found in Kavitha's bag. I have asked them to talk again with me tomorrow afternoon.

qa.q: Where was Nikita standing?
qa.a: Near the open door, well back from Kavitha.

qa.q: How did Nikita seem to feel while Kavitha shouted?
qa.a: She seemed shaken and frightened, yet chose to keep her voice quiet.

qa.q: What made Nikita's response wise?
qa.a: Keeping distance and refusing to shout back kept things safe and gave Kavitha room to calm down.

qa.q: What was behind Kavitha's shouting?
qa.a: She was stressed and anxious about her exam the next day, which came out as anger about the charger.

grounding: Shows a young adult being shouted at by a roommate, keeping distance and a quiet voice, which keeps things safe and lets the other person deflate.

subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
passage:
Tuesday
What a night. I came back from the library and Hansa exploded at me before I could even put my bag down. 'You never clean! You leave your stuff everywhere! I can't live like this!' I just froze at first. My heart was hammering and part of me wanted to scream right back, list every dish she's left in the sink. But I remembered the last time we fought, when it got so loud the neighbour came. So I stayed by the door, took a breath, and said quietly, 'Okay. I hear you're angry. I'm not going to shout.' She shouted a bit more. I just stood there, quiet. Then her face crumpled. She sat on her bed and said her internship had rejected her today. I sat down too, not too close. We'll talk about the cleaning tomorrow. Pooja

qa.q: What had happened to Hansa's internship?
qa.a: It had rejected her that day.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling when Hansa started shouting?
qa.a: Pooja felt shocked and frozen, with a hammering heart and an urge to shout back.

qa.q: Which of Pooja's choices helped the most?
qa.a: Staying by the door and speaking quietly without matching the volume, which let Hansa's anger run out.

qa.q: How might Hansa feel the next day?
qa.a: Hansa may feel embarrassed about exploding and grateful that Pooja stayed calm.

grounding: Shows a young adult shouted at by a roommate who keeps distance and refuses to match the volume, which keeps things safe and lets the other person deflate.

subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
passage: In the polytechnic hostel at Satara, Dinesh burst into Chinmay's room at midnight. 'You complained about the mess food? You made the warden cancel our cricket?' He was shouting, spit flying, fists tight. Chinmay's heart slammed. A hot wish to shout back, even shove, rose in his chest. Instead he stood up slowly, stepped back to keep the bed between them, and said quietly, 'I'll talk, but not like this.' Dinesh yelled again. Chinmay didn't raise his voice. After a minute Dinesh's shoulders dropped; he muttered something and left. Chinmay sat on the bed, shaking. In the morning he told Usha Ma'am, the warden, about the midnight visit, and she met them both that afternoon.

qa.q: What did Chinmay keep between himself and Dinesh?
qa.a: The bed.

qa.q: What did Chinmay feel when Dinesh burst in shouting?
qa.a: He felt shocked and afraid, heart slamming, with a hot urge to shout back or shove.

qa.q: What kept the situation safe?
qa.a: Chinmay kept his distance, spoke quietly and refused to match the volume, then told the warden the next morning.

qa.q: How might Dinesh have felt when Chinmay didn't shout back?
qa.a: Dinesh's anger probably had nothing to push against, so he deflated and left.

grounding: A young man shouted at in a hostel feels shock and an urge to hit back, but keeps distance and refuses to match the volume.
